Activating a missing edge with the strongest op gives a bigger gain than replacing an existing op.
A none on the first edge cuts the node 1 path, so adding a conv there gains more than a swap would.
Reviving a dead edge with a 3x3 conv matters more than upgrading an edge that already carries an op.
Connecting node 1 to node 2 with a conv adds depth and paths, which beats the gain from replacing an existing op.
Upgrading 1x1 to 3x3 is a small gain compared with the average gain over all other ops being replaced.
Skip replacing none adds a residual path, while skip replacing a conv loses accuracy.
Swapping a 3x3 conv for a skip loses capacity, which is worse than swapping a weaker op for a skip.
Removing a 3x3 conv edge costs more accuracy than removing a weak op like pooling or skip.
